newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end banner year with gains.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end banner year with gains.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed out a banner year on Tuesday with gains but near the session lows after several U.S. economic figures hit international markets.

The initial advances could have been window dressing ahead of the new year, dealers said. Some said dollar weakness was the primary reason Madrid stocks, which had set several record highs in 1996, slid back near the end.
The general index rose 1.35 points, 0.30 percent, to 444.77 after hitting a high of 448.77 and a low of 444.67. The Ibex-35 gained 9.82 points, 0.19 percent, to 5,154.77.
Trading volume was healthy with 40 million shares traded, much of which dealers attributed to year-end investment and tax housekeeping rather than a sign of particular interest in the bourse.
Electricity shares led the gains as the market expected falling interest rates in the coming year to help the heavily indebted sector and offset cuts in electricity prices.
Partly state-owned Endesa soared, gaining 200 pesetas, 2.21 percent, to 9,240.
